On the authority of Abū ʿAmr—and it is a: Sufyān ibn ʿAbdillāh (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: “I said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me something about Islam that I will not need to ask anyone else about but you. He said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.” Reported by Muslim.
“Tell me something about Islam”: about its religion and its law.
Qawlan (“something”): comprehensive of the meanings of the religion, which I can be content with and act upon.
Istaqim (“be upright”): hold to doing what is commanded and refrain from everything forbidden.
The command to be upright (istiqāmah), which is being correct and balanced in all praiseworthy words, deeds and intentions.
Avoiding what is unlawful and everything contrary to the Sharīʿah, in word, deed or belief.
It is permissible to give a ruling in summary form if the person understands it without detail.
The hadith affirms general wording and acting upon all that it includes.

The Companion who narrates this hadith tells us that he asked the Prophet ﷺ to teach him what he needed for his religion: a saying that comprehends and encompasses the meanings of Islam, plain and clear, needing no explanation, and sufficient so that with it he would need to ask no one else.
The Messenger ﷺ commanded him to persevere in faith, and then to be balanced and upright in what faith requires: carrying out the commands, the recommended and the obligatory,

and avoiding the prohibitions, the unlawful and the disliked. If he acts on this, he is saved and successful in this world and the Hereafter. The Mighty Qurʾān has mentioned the great favour for whoever believes in Allah and then is upright; the Exalted said:

“Indeed, those who say ‘Our Lord is Allah’ and then remain upright—the angels will descend upon them, [saying]: Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive the good news of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request, as a welcome from One Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful” [Fuṣṣilat 41:30–32].
The printed text reads لمعانق الإسلام, evidently for لمعاني الإسلام (“the meanings of Islam”).
Setting your affairs right comes back to character, / so straighten the soul with good character and you will be upright.
My son, be upright, for the stick's roots grow / straight, and if it bends, what covers it bends too.
